assetInventory.method: Declared asset registries with real PNG/hash/dimension/alpha checks; shared sheets counted once. This does not certify source-frame fidelity.

evidenceRules.missing: An authored capability or dedicated animation/script is absent; a generic rendering fallback may still draw successfully.
evidenceRules.adaptation: An authored runtime sequence, generated bitmap, reused pose, transformed static layer or procedural effect. Its existence does not prove source fidelity.
evidenceRules.verified: Requires independently retained source reference, frame/scene comparison and explicit validation. No such certification is inferred from a name, profile, bitmap, or passing tests.
evidenceRules.bitmapEvidence: Binding analysis below inspects routing metadata only. Exact repeated RGBA cells are measured separately by auditCombatCharacterAnimations.mjs.

abilities.heuristicNote: The original broad Guard suffix includes 118 concrete defense names requiring review, not 118 confirmed generic actions.
abilities.strictDefinition: simple/secondary: original placeholder expressions; defense: Signature Guard|defensive action or exact hero.name + " Guard".

entries.sourceWork: Metal Gear Solid (1998)
entries.sourceReference: Adult Solid Snake uses the SOCOM Mk23, Nikita and cardboard box. His unarmed punch/punch/kick combo is condensed into one contact impact. Advanced CQC of other protagonists/eras and damaging chaff are not added.

entries.sourceWork: Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance (2013)
entries.sourceReference: Cyborg Raiden uses a high-frequency blade, Ninja Run and physical parry. Zandatsu Overdrive is the project label for an adapted close blade sequence: no instant kill, life extraction or distant area strike is implied.

entries.sourceWork: Metal Gear Solid (1998) / Metal Gear Solid 2 (2001)
entries.sourceReference: Hal Emmerich provides Codec, technical analysis and later Philanthropy intelligence. Terminal commands provide allied information support only. Philanthropy Upload and Metal Gear Data Hack are project labels, not canonical damaging attacks; no beam, infection, enemy HP loss or healing is created.

entries.sourceWork: Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (1983)
entries.sourceReference: Adult Luke wears black and uses his green lightsaber. Force push is adapted as a bounded local force impulse. His close saber sequence is one timed impact, not a damaging Jedi mind beam or an invented telepathic attack.

entries.sourceWork: Star Wars original trilogy (1977–1983)
entries.sourceReference: Armored Darth Vader uses his red lightsaber and telekinetic Force choke. Choke is a bounded single-target damaging command without a forced instant kill or invented infection. The Imperial March is music, not an attack.

entries.sourceWork: Star Wars: A New Hope (1977)
entries.sourceReference: Han uses a DL-44 heavy blaster and practical cover. His personal super is one accurate blaster shot. The Kessel Run and Millennium Falcon are not a remote area power, and cover provides no magical carbonite barrier.

nativePresentationEntries.sourceReference: Lion Heart is Squall's final Renzokuken finishing technique unlocked by the Lion Heart gunblade. The ultimate gunblade is an explicit equipment adaptation for this combat sequence; clothing follows the local FFVIII Squall reference.

Wishing Star is a Combine Limit Break performed together with Angelo. It is not Angel Wing. The partnered leap and star-like motion are a condensed combat adaptation, not a reproduction of the complete original cinematic. Angelo is represented as a brown-and-white medium collie-like dog, with no invented fantasy anatomy.

Quistis uses a whip and Shockwave Pulsar is her strongest Blue Magic, learned with Dark Matter. The gravitational energy buildup and shockwave are adapted to compact side-view frames, without turning them into Laser Eye or inventing a summon.

Seifer's original FFVIII identity uses his long light-gray/white coat with red cross motifs and the Hyperion gunblade. No Mercy is his Fire Cross Limit Break. The local black fur-collar jacket is a known reference mistake, explicitly corrected rather than copied.

Normal orange Gravity Gun secondary projects a small metal crate; the super alone is the blue Citadel tool redirecting a captured Combine energy ball. One compact gameplay impact replaces original lethality. Source reference shows old wrong minigun and is used only for HEV/face.
Barney wears originalHL2 Civil Protection clothing and uses a pulse rifle. His coordination secondary is a support adaptation. No Black Mesa uniform or invented evacuation damage.
HL2 Alyx uses her own automatic pistol and physical multitool. Door opening gives bounded support, no offensive hacking magic or Half-Life:Alyx gravity gloves.

Eli is a scientist and Resistance coordinator; briefing is an authored bounded ally buff, not a canonical named attack. No handheld energy gun. Left below-knee prosthesis preserved; no actor portrait.

Selected laboratory support is a bounded ally guard adapting safe-transfer preparation; not a claim that Kleiner creates handheld shields. His source occasionally shows a shotgun but this chosen kit and art are non-offensive laboratory work.
T-60b Brotherhood Danse uses a laser rifle. Source weapons verified on a page actually opened; finite single-target gameplay shot, personal power-armor guard, no Liberty Prime summon.
Default Fallout4 Nick uses a pipe revolver pistol, not a standard .44. Calibre is intentionally not asserted. Detective information is allied support rather than an offensive scan.

Dogmeat remains a natural quadruped companion with one close bite/hold gameplay impact. Ear-tip height110, withers80 and body-length170 calibration are independent of bipedBODY190; one source-wide scale preserves low crouches/leaps. No weapon or humanoid anatomy.

Piper default weapon is the10mm pistol. Publick Occurrences super preserves the previous zero-damage allied information buff; numerical attack bonus is an explicit gameplay adaptation of reporting, not healing or the source experience perk.

Preston’s actual weapon is a crank-charged laser musket. Its super shape is corrected from an unverified penetrating line to one finite single-target projectile. Physical command secondary remains support, no artillery summon.

Neo from The Matrix Reloaded (2003), adult slim tall man, short black hair, clean-shaven face, narrow black sunglasses, CLOSED long BLACK high-collar buttoned cassock-style coat down to the calves, black trousers and black boots. His coat must be closed over his torso, no open trench, visible belt harness, weapons, guns or code magic. Preserve this specific film identity; correct the old reference’s open coat. Empty-handed martial combination: settles in a bent-knee guard, steps forward with a straight palm strike, pivots into a controlled high side kick, draws the leg back into guard. Four distinct full-body poses; no opponents, impact burst, flying projectile, giant green explosion or body beam. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Trinity from The Matrix Reloaded (2003), adult slim athletic woman, short slicked-back black hair, narrow black sunglasses, fitted BLACK leather high-neck zip jacket and matching black leather trousers, black boots. TWO real compact black Beretta 92-series pistols, one per hand, complete barrels and human hands. No motorcycle, anime redesign or revealing costume. Physical dual-pistol sequence: raises both real Beretta pistols from low-ready, aims toward screen right, a small LOCAL amber muzzle flash at the barrel exit in THIRD cell only with shifted arms/recoil, lowers both pistols to recover in FOURTH cell. No laser beam, distant bullet, target impact or magic kiss. Keep both pistols separate and anatomically held. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Morpheus from The Matrix Reloaded (2003), bald Black adult man, strong face, distinctive small oval mirrored PENCE-NEZ sunglasses clipped to nose WITHOUT temple arms, long dark purple-black textured crocodile-pattern leather coat, dark purple tailored vest/shirt and dark trousers, heavy black shoes. His freeway-sequence KATANA is a complete thin curved steel sword with normal hilt and guard held in real hands. No staff, cane, futuristic firearm, huge fantasy sword or red pill power. Physical katana sequence: brings the katana into a two-handed ready position, steps into a diagonal cut, completes the blade arc with twisted torso and bent knee, returns the whole sword to a safe low guard. Four different poses; full blade remains inside each cell, no detached slash projectile, glowing code or impact explosion. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Smith from The Matrix Reloaded (2003), adult white man, slicked-back short brown hair with receding hairline, narrow rectangular black sunglasses, dark charcoal-green business suit with jacket, white collared shirt, BLACK necktie, polished black shoes. BOTH EMPTY HANDS. The freed Smith has no earpiece. No clone, coat, pistol, laser, body code beam or later Resurrections redesign. Unarmed physical combination: sets both fists, steps forward with a straight right punch, rotates shoulders into a second body-height punch, recovers into his squared fighting stance. Distinct arm and leg placements in all four cells. One body per cell, no extra Smith, green explosion or magical duplication. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Seraph from The Matrix Reloaded (2003), adult East Asian martial guardian, short neatly combed black hair, slim athletic build, LIGHT CREAM/OFF-WHITE long-sleeved mandarin-collar Chinese jacket with short front frog/button closures, BLACK loose trousers, plain black martial shoes. Clean face, natural dark eyes, no glasses for this tea-house martial sequence. Correct the old reference’s all-black jacket to the light cream jacket. Both hands empty; no katana, gold armor, fire or emitted firewall. Unarmed tea-house guardian combination: sets an open-palm guard, advances with a palm strike, pivots into a controlled waist-high side kick, retracts the leg and returns to guard. Each pose differs. No opponent, body beam, golden explosion, fire, shield disk or emitted code. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Colonel Jack O’Neill from Stargate SG-1 SEASON FOUR (2000–2001), adult older white man, short graying brown hair, clean-shaven face, olive-green military field shirt and fatigues, black plain tactical vest with practical pouches, SG-1/USAF patches on upper sleeves, black boots. NO sci-fi plate armor, glowing blue parts or futuristic rifle. Real BLACK FN P90 with top horizontal translucent magazine and thumbhole stock, human right hand on grip, left hand supporting front. Not Kurt Russell’s 1994 colonel. Physical P90 cover burst: lifts the compact actual FN P90 from low-ready, aims forward toward screen right using both hands, third pose has small local AMBER muzzle flash at the genuine short barrel with bodily recoil, lowers gun in fourth pose. No body beam, gate explosion, huge distant tracer, portal or orbital strike. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Teal’c from Stargate SG-1 SEASON FOUR (2000–2001), tall muscular bald Black adult man, dark brown skin, gold Apophis symbol on FOREHEAD, clean-shaven, olive/gray-green SG-1 field fatigues and dark plain tactical vest, black boots. NO ornate gold Jaffa torso armor, hair or later season goatee. His long Goa’uld JAFFA STAFF WEAPON is a functional dark bronze staff with recognizable split oval cobra-like emitting HEAD at its forward end; not a wizard trident, spear or laser rifle. Keep complete staff and both ends within every cell. Jaffa staff firing sequence: brings the complete staff to shoulder/waist level, aims the OPEN oval emitting head toward screen right, third pose shows ONE SMALL local orange plasma flare at the actual open staff head and slight recoil, fourth lowers the complete staff safely. No long beam, detached plasma ball traveling across the tile, distant explosion, army or magic uprising. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Major Samantha Carter from Stargate SG-1 SEASON FOUR (2000–2001), adult white woman, short neat BLOND pixie hair, no hat or glasses, olive-green military field shirt/fatigues with SG-1 sleeve patch, black plain tactical vest with pouches, black boots. Real compact BLACK FN P90 with TOP horizontal magazine and thumbhole stock, anatomically held in both hands. Correct old reference’s futuristic armor and glowing laser rifle. No naquadah magic, bodysuit or later uniform. Physical P90 cover burst: shoulders the actual P90 while stepping into a firm stance, aims its short barrel toward screen right, third pose has one small local amber muzzle flash and recoil, fourth lowers the rifle to safe low-ready. No calculation glyphs, glowing hands, body beam, distant tracer or large target impact. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Dr Daniel Jackson from Stargate SG-1 SEASON FOUR (2000–2001), UNASCENDED HUMAN adult white archaeologist, short light brown hair, thin-rimmed rectangular glasses, olive-green field shirt/fatigues, brown/olive practical field vest with pouches, black boots. Props are a small ordinary paper NOTEBOOK and handheld/shoulder RADIO. No rifle attack, glyph gun, glowing tablet, staff, angelic aura, light-body ascension or later long hair. Preserve his calm scholarly face. Zero-damage field information support: opens a small paper notebook in his left hand, observes screen right and points at an ordinary note with right index finger, speaks into a real small radio, lowers radio and closes notebook. Four distinct natural human full-body poses, calm and purposeful. No emitted glyphs, beams, energy shield, magical buff halo, translation projectile or glowing hands. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

General George Hammond from Stargate SG-1 SEASON FOUR (2000–2001), older stocky white man, bald head with slight gray side hair, calm round face, USAF BLUE SERVICE DRESS jacket and matching trousers, light blue shirt, dark tie, modest real ribbons/badges, black formal shoes. Hold an ordinary small black RADIO and/or paper briefing folder. NO pistol, rifle, tactical plate armor, futuristic device, glowing shield or later action-hero physique. Correct old reference’s gun to ordinary command equipment. Zero-damage radio extraction authorization: raises a small real radio in his right hand, listens and looks toward screen right, speaks into radio while his left hand gives a clear ordinary directional order, lowers radio and relaxes left arm. Four distinct complete body poses. No portal, weapon, muzzle flash, beams, holographic troops, healing glow or magical shield bubble. All timing, targeting and finite gameplay effects are adapted; no official1:1 frames are certified.

Buffy Summers, adult Slayer in season7 (2002–2003). Shoulder-length straight blonde hair, plain black sleeveless tank top, burgundy/maroon fitted full-length trousers, black shoes. Natural sharpened WOODEN STAKE in anatomical right hand only when preparing/attacking; small stake holster at right waist when hands free. No Scythe, no red amulet, no firearm or magic. Same mature natural proportions as reference, not chibi. Preserve viewed black top/burgundy trouser identity; add the actual wooden stake required by the selected actions, exclude later Scythe and amulet.

Willow Rosenberg, adult auburn-haired woman in Buffy season7, controlled protective witchcraft, NOT Dark Willow. Shoulder-length auburn hair, soft purple cardigan over a modest dark green top, full-length charcoal trousers and flat brown shoes. Normal eyes and skin; no black hair/veins. Empty hands, no gun, staff, glowing amulet or overalls. Old salopette is an earlier broad cue; choose ordinary adult season7 cardigan and trousers. No Dark Willow, finale white-hair Slayer activation or gun.

Rupert Giles, middle-aged human Watcher in Buffy season7. Short receding brown/grey hair, rectangular wire glasses, brown tweed jacket over grey waistcoat and pale shirt, dark red tie, brown trousers and sensible brown shoes. Physical wooden-and-dark-metal CROSSBOW with horizontal bow limbs and visible bolt rail; held in TWO hands. No gun, magical book laser or huge fantasy bow. Preserve human bespectacled brown-jacket Watcher identity but add a complete physical crossbow; no book beam or gun.

Xander Harris, ordinary adult human in Buffy season7 after Spike chip removal and BEFORE Caleb eye injury, both eyes intact. Short dark brown hair, open dark blue overshirt over light grey T-shirt, brown trousers, black-and-white trainers. Empty hands. No pistol, rifle, magic circle, aura, superhuman muscles or eye patch. Remove the old invented pistol, muzzle flashes and glowing gun aura. Select the season7 interval before his eye injury; all actions are ordinary cover instructions.

Spike, adult soul-restored vampire in Buffy season7, after chip removed and after Get It Done duster retrieval, before final amulet. Short slicked-back PLATINUM BLOND hair, pale skin, long worn BLACK LEATHER DUSTER, BLACK T-SHIRT, dark jeans, black combat boots. Empty fists. NO red/gold amulet, NO sword/stake/gun, no fire, wings, glowing veins, fangs closeup or vampire transformation. Remove old red amulet, swords and firecasting entirely; keep platinium hair and complete black leather duster. Physical fists/kicks only.

Ron Weasley, sixth-year student Half-Blood Prince FILM2009, approximately16–17, tall slim fully clothed natural teen proportions, not chibi. Short tousled GINGER hair, freckles, white collared shirt, grey school V-neck pullover, Gryffindor RED/GOLD tie, full-length black trousers, black school shoes, open BLACK SCHOOL ROBE dark red lining. Thin wooden WAND in anatomical right hand: slender branch-like stick, NO trigger or gun barrel. No firearm or pistol anywhere. The old reference wrongly draws a handgun. Replace it completely with a slim wooden wand held as a wand, keeping red hair and HP6 uniform. No gun-shaped handle.

Albus Dumbledore as in Half-Blood Prince FILM2009 (Michael Gambon version), elderly with long SILVER WHITE hair and long white beard, small half-moon glasses. SILVER-GREY embroidered full-length robe and long grey-silver outer robe, soft grey tassel cap; brown shoes peeking below hem. Wooden Elder Wand in RIGHT hand, right hand visibly darkened/blackened from the ring curse WITHOUT open wounds or gore. No purple/gold early-film robe, giant staff, gun, alchemist machine or youthful body. Correct old purple/gold robe to documented HP6 silver-grey costume; retain elderly beard/glasses and thin wand, no gun or huge purple laser. Dark right hand is source-specific, not a new injury mechanic.

Sheppard carries a real FN P90 during Atlantis field missions; Sateda depicts him firing that weapon. Route calls coordinate allies and cover is personal protection. The super is one finite P90 shot at the selected target, not a ship laser, mental ray or Puddle Jumper summon.

McKay diagnoses Ancient technology through real consoles and portable computing equipment. The selected tablet readout and protective guidance adapt that technical role; they neither emit offensive energy nor heal biological injuries. Other scenes may arm McKay, but these selected actions remain technical support.

Teyla practises Athosian bantos fighting with one or two wooden rods; the name is used in season3 Sunday. The chosen two-stick physical combination has a single close-range gameplay impact. The rods do not become swords, laser blades or ranged spells.

Ronon uses a compact Satedan particle-magnum sidearm and physical close combat. Sateda shows him firing energy pistols and Progeny shows his blaster being drawn, set and holstered. The finite red bolt leaves the actual gun opening; no Wraith power, giant revolver, body mutation or area blast is added.

Weir leads and coordinates the human Atlantis expedition before her later nanite fate. The radio carries spoken protective instructions and diplomatic planning. No gun is fired by radio, no nanite attack is granted, and no healing or magical shield projectile is invented.

Rush studies Destiny interfaces and computes the ship systems using real controls and notes. Air shows his database work during the life-support crisis. The information advantage is a bounded allied buff, without personal Ancient beams, forced ship fire, clock manipulation or healing.

Young commands the stranded crew and assigns field missions. His selected radio instructions protect real allied targets; other scenes with weapons do not turn this support profile into a shooting action. Protective orders are bounded guard without HP restoration or a ship weapon.

Greer is a Black US Marine using physical firearms in season1. Both G36K and M4 are documented; this presentation selects his black M4A1 carbine, matching the scene in which he shows Eli the rifle. His finite bullet and cover orders do not create laser beams, grenades or Kino ammunition.

Chloe is a human civilian during the selected season1 role. She listens and relays practical instructions through an ordinary radio, guiding companions to cover. No later alien mutation, offensive data burst, telepathy, weapon or medical power is transferred into this kit.

Lieutenant Scott carries a black HK G36K with an integrated carry-handle optic during season1 field missions. This is distinct from the UMP he also uses in Water. Rifle fire remains one finite selected-target impact, and reconnaissance is an information buff, never a Kino fired as a projectile.

Korben Dallas, film1997, fights with an ordinary handheld pistol and his physical training. The ZF-1 demonstration belongs to Zorg; no rocket launcher, taxi door, explosion power or summoned vehicle is assigned to Korben.

Leeloo uses physical punches and kicks in the1997 film. This version selects the orange suspenders, white shirt and gold trousers. The final ritual needs the four activated stones and love: none of that context is supplied here, so no autonomous fifth-element beam, divine-language explosion or body light is invented.

Ruby Rhod is the human broadcast host of the1997 film, with his actual microphone and production communications. Passing information is an authored team buff. His voice does not cause physical damage, sonic attacks, explosions, healing or magical morale rays.

Jean-Baptiste Emanuel Zorg demonstrates the physical multifunction ZF-1 in the1997 film. Its barrel and integrated rocket equipment are portable gun components, not powers or a pistol assigned to Korben. The selected super is a conventional burst from the ZF-1, condensed to one accepted simulated projectile impact.

Vito Cornelius, film1997, is the priest who knows and explains the guardians and elemental ritual. His selected actions communicate instructions and safe movement. No activated stones, staff attack, healing miracle, elemental shield or fifth-element beam is created by his gestures.

Arthur Pendragon in Kaamelott LivreIII2005 is a trained human king and swordsman. Excalibur is held, parried and swung physically. This authored sequence does not turn royal instructions, the Grail quest, sword light or weariness into a damaging area power.

Perceval in Kaamelott LivreIII2005 is a human knight. This selected supporting role uses a cautious physical guard and a regrouping signal, with equipment held safely. Confused rules, catchphrases, luck and misunderstandings do not strike enemies or create magical protection.

Karadoc in Kaamelott LivreIII2005 carries, checks and shares ordinary provisions. These zero-damage coordination buffs adapt his concern for food and logistics. Eating is not instantaneous magical HP restoration, an offensive feast, a summoned table or supernatural nourishment.

Léodagan in Kaamelott LivreIII2005 is the human warrior king of Carmélide. The selected charge and sword cut are physical. Orders support the team without harming through words; no firearm, crossbow cannon, magical fortification or beam belongs to this equipment.

Lancelot in Kaamelott LivreIII2005 wears his pale knightly tunic and brown leather harness, with fair nape-length hair and a physical straight sword. These attacks and parries stay within that period, before later dark armour, masks, faction costume or invented holy projectiles.

The Jungle Hunter is the hunter of Predator1987. His two wrist blades and shoulder plasma caster belong to that film. This selected kit uses physical wrist-blade cuts and a finite close thrust; the smart disc and combi-stick of City Hunter are not transferred to him. Camouflage and the self-destruct device are not made into a damaging fog trial or an arena-wide explosion.

City Hunter in Predator2 1990 carries the telescoping combi-stick and the smart disc. The chosen native sequence is a physical combi-stick thrust with an existing held spear, not a supernatural trophy hunt, light beam, invented returning disc flight or summoned alien weapon. All three selected attacks preserve the same held spear.

Dutch Schaefer in Predator1987 uses an M16A1 with an M203 underbarrel launcher. The chosen kit keeps the ordinary rifle and its conventional ballistic shots. Blain carries the minigun; Dutch does not receive it. Get to the chopper is a command rather than a damaging power, and no helicopter body, giant explosion, mud teleport or alien plasma caster is created.

Anna Gonsalves in Predator1987 is the rescued human who observes, warns and follows an escape route. The selected protective kit adapts visible pointing and regrouping as bounded zero-damage support. She carries no invented gun, knife, alien weapon, force field or magical healing item; her speech and gestures do not hurt enemies.

Billy Sole in Predator1987 is a human tracker carrying a large machete. The selected version retains his field gear before the bridge scene. His cuts are physical and the finishing presentation is a solo controlled swing. No self-cutting, blood ritual, spiritual attack, supernatural awareness damage or opponent execution is depicted or calculated.

Mac Eliot in Predator1987 uses the conventional belt-fed M60 machine gun. Its stock, barrel and ammunition belt stay physical; the super adapts a controlled burst to one accepted simulated projectile impact. It does not hand him Blain’s minigun, an alien laser, explosive rage or a remote jungle-wide strike.

Mike Harrigan in Predator2 1990 is an LAPD human detective using an ordinary handgun. This version keeps his pale short-sleeved shirt, trousers and holster. The selected attack is a deliberate ballistic shot, not the City Hunter’s disc, a trophy-hunt area effect, a futuristic rifle or a police command turned into damage.

Greyback Elder appears at the end of Predator2 1990 and offers Harrigan the Raphael Adolini1715 flintlock pistol as a trophy. His presentation preserves an unfired antique and a composed recognition gesture. The secondary and super are bounded support adaptations, not a magical elder aura, plasma cannon, automatic rifle or invented discharge of the trophy pistol. A basic claw motion remains separate.

Naru in Prey2022 is an adult Comanche human hunter. Her practical deerskin clothing and rope-tethered tomahawk remain human equipment. The selected sequence is a short hatchet cut and rope retrieval rather than a supernatural hunt reversal, an alien weapon, magical rope, dog summon or distant axe flight. Her old erroneous alien silhouette is excluded from image-generation reference inputs.

Royce in Predators2010 carries the conventional AA-12 automatic shotgun with its drum magazine. This selected shot keeps that practical firearm and human tactical gear. He does not gain the Yautja’s plasma caster, a supernatural Super Predator ambush, an M60 belt feed, a world-sized explosion or an invented summoned hunter.

Fry is an ordinary Planet Express delivery boy in the original Fox run. A parcel relay and safe-position signal are bounded coordination adaptations, not ammunition, a parcel explosion, a laser attack or an invented psychic power. His red jacket, white shirt, blue jeans and orange hair are fixed to this period.

Leela is a skilled physical martial artist and Planet Express pilot. This short punch-and-kick combination uses her limbs and athletic guard, not a gun, laser or eye beam. One accepted close contact resolves damage; generated drawings do not add extra hits. Her single central eye remains a single eye.

Bender is the gray bending robot from the original Fox run. Articulated arms, hands and a short physical charge stay mechanical. His chest compartment does not spawn weapons, his eyes do not fire beams and this authored contact sequence does not invent a plasma cannon.

Amy is a Planet Express engineering intern in the original Fox period. Examining an ordinary handheld diagnostic pad and communicating a finding give bounded coordination buffs. She has no damaging scanner, gun, healing ray or magical repair power. The pink tracksuit and black bob haircut remain her normal outfit.

Hermes is the human bureaucrat of Planet Express. He sorts actual papers, checks a clipboard and gives work instructions. These zero-damage coordination effects do not turn paperwork, limbo or spoken orders into lasers, physical projectiles, instant healing or supernatural barriers.

Dr John Zoidberg is the red Decapodian in a white medical coat, mint shirt and gray trousers. This version uses cautious advice and withdrawal signals rather than claiming reliable human treatment. No HP regeneration, healing magic, claw projectile or beam is supplied by these gestures.

Season2 Rick uses an ordinary compact science-fiction pistol as the selected damaging equipment. The distinct green portal gun is a transit device and is not used as a damaging blaster. The support action communicates a safe route without teleporting units, splitting reality or creating a Microverse explosion. His source-era white coat, pale cyan shirt and brown trousers remain unchanged.

Season2 Summer wears a coral-pink sleeveless top, white trousers and black shoes, with orange ponytail. This supporting version communicates a regrouping route. It does not borrow the season3 wasteland costume, rifle, psychic effects or a post-apocalyptic area attack. Her instructions do not inflict damage.

Birdperson is his biological season2 version before Phoenixperson. His natural brown feathered wings fold into a physical protective stance, adapted into a bounded guard without adding flight, teleportation, healing or a supernatural force field. Cybernetic wings, implants, laser eyes and the later Phoenixperson weapons are excluded.

entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Dr John Zoidberg
entries.sourceReference: Dr John Zoidberg is the red Decapodian in a white medical coat, mint shirt and gray trousers. This version uses cautious advice and withdrawal signals rather than claiming reliable human treatment. No HP regeneration, healing magic, claw projectile or beam is supplied by these gestures.

entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Rick Sanchez humain
entries.sourceReference: Season2 Rick uses an ordinary compact science-fiction pistol as the selected damaging equipment. The distinct green portal gun is a transit device and is not used as a damaging blaster. The support action communicates a safe route without teleporting units, splitting reality or creating a Microverse explosion. His source-era white coat, pale cyan shirt and brown trousers remain unchanged.

entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Summer Smith avant la tenue post-apocalyptique de saison 3
entries.sourceReference: Season2 Summer wears a coral-pink sleeveless top, white trousers and black shoes, with orange ponytail. This supporting version communicates a regrouping route. It does not borrow the season3 wasteland costume, rifle, psychic effects or a post-apocalyptic area attack. Her instructions do not inflict damage.

entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Birdperson avant sa transformation en Phoenixperson
entries.sourceReference: Birdperson is his biological season2 version before Phoenixperson. His natural brown feathered wings fold into a physical protective stance, adapted into a bounded guard without adding flight, teleportation, healing or a supernatural force field. Cybernetic wings, implants, laser eyes and the later Phoenixperson weapons are excluded.

entries.sourceReference: Bastion’s beacon defines a safe route: deployment, alignment and protective planes, never an explosion.

entries.key: Nexus de Convergence::Drone de Suture::Drone de Suture
entries.sourceReference: Loom’s drone maintains an ally’s signature: hover, medical link, stabilization and return to the caller.

entries.key: Nexus de Convergence::Reflet Non Remplace::Reflet Non Remplace
entries.sourceReference: Tessera manifests a possible reflection without replacing a person: a mirrored arrival and refracted proof, then dissolution.

entries.key: Nexus de Convergence::Sonde de Retour::Sonde de Retour
entries.sourceReference: Nadir’s probe verifies a route in both directions: outbound scan, measured contact and a visible retraced return.
Halo Pelican gunship support: heavy approach, undercarriage firing pass and continued flight out of the arena.
Dog’s physical assistance uses a robot leap and grounded force, followed by a bounding retreat; no energy detonation.
Portal sentry: vertical placement, visible red targeting line, a ballistic burst and folding withdrawal.
PAYDAY’s deployable sentry is placed on the floor, aims mechanically and fires bullets; it does not walk or cast a beam.
The existing page deployment is represented by placed pages, paper motion and camera-static interference, without a fire or magic blast.
BFG-9000: capacitor charge, one traveling plasma sphere and branching green energy arcs; a single gameplay impact remains authoritative.
May’s Great Yamada Attack brings the whale across the scene in an arcing passage with a water surge, then carries it out.
Final Fantasy VII Hellfire: Ifrit arrives, gathers fire and sends a ground-reaching flame wave into the opposing formation.
Final Fantasy VII Diamond Dust: Shiva gathers cold, encases targets in ice and shatters the ice before disappearing.
Final Fantasy VII Megaflare: Bahamut descends above the battlefield, charges at its mouth and releases the charged ray into the targets.

entries.key: Sonic::Tails et le Tornado::Tornado Machine Gun
entries.sourceReference: Sonic Adventure’s Tornado: a banked airplane approach, machine-gun pass and rising departure, without a teleporting ground entrance.
Star Platinum manifests by Jotaro, closes to punch range, performs a visible fist barrage and withdraws to the caller.

entries.key: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure::Hermit Purple::Hermit Purple — Hamon
entries.sourceReference: Hermit Purple grows from Joseph as thorny purple vines; a gold Hamon pulse travels along the vine and retracts with it.
Gold Experience manifests beside Giorno, advances to its selected target, punches in a compact barrage and returns.
Imani’s project-owned Ghostline uprising spreads coordinated drone/signal links; its technology is not a ghost-shaped magical explosion.

entries.key: The Aether Crown::Mutinerie des Cieux::Mutinerie des Cieux
entries.sourceReference: Elara’s project-owned corsair command brings airborne allied craft along an advancing sky route with coordinated deck fire.
Bram Quill’s autonomous valve drone hovers, builds pressure and vents directed steam, then returns without exploding.

entries.key: Meridian Clockwork::Faucon à Ressort::Faucon à Ressort
entries.sourceReference: Lio’s spring-driven mechanical falcon winds up, dives along a clockwork arc and visibly homes back toward its operator.

entries.key: Aegea: War of the Moirai::Forge des Cent Boucliers::Forge des Cent Boucliers
entries.sourceReference: Doros’s project-owned forge constructs a bronze shield formation: assembling plates, a closing line and orderly withdrawal.

entries.key: Tawantinsuyu: The Split Sun::Message des Quatre Quartiers::Message des Quatre Quartiers
entries.sourceReference: Killa Mayu’s four-quarter message is a courier relay with linked route points and traveling signals, not an explosive summoned army.

wave16PersistentProtectionEntries.sourceWork: Cuphead: The Delicious Last Course (2022), Ms. Chalice Super Art II — Shield Pal
wave16PersistentProtectionEntries.sourceReference: Small pointed golden shield, red-pink heart inset with two black oval/pie-cut eyes, two complete white feathered wings at the upper sides, black cartoon ink outline. No arms, legs, mouth, insect body, Chalice body, generic blue energy bubble or empty force-field ring. New pixel-art drawings, not official frames. The source hit/departure references distort and disperse the heart; the bounded engine withdraws a complete familiar before hiding it so every retained native cell has the whole source entity. Timings .4s arrival/.56s guard loop/.4s absorb/.4s departure are explicit engine sampling, not certified source timings.
